title: Modeling Inhibited Growth
problem: An engineer observed that the growth of the number of solar panels installed at a facility is directly proportional to the difference between the facility’s maximum number of solar panels and the current number installed. Let $P(t)$ be the number of solar panels, measured in panels, and let $t\ge 0$ be the time in years. If the maximum number of solar panels the facility can support is $240$ panels, which differential equation could be used to model the number of solar panels installed? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral
problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x+y\le 2,\,0\le y-x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 3}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y-x,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}2(x+y){e}^{y-x}\,dV={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$

title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le {x}^{2}+y\le 2,\,-1\le x\le 1,\,1\le z\le 4}.
$$

 

Given the change of variables

$$
u={x}^{2}+y,\,v=2x+z,\,w=z,

{∭}_{R}(2x+z)\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+y)\,dV={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{6}{\int }_{1}^{4}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$

title: Performing a Change of Variables in a Triple Integral
problem:

$$

$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=x+3y,\,v=z-3y,\,w=z,
$$

$$
{∭}_{R}{cos}^{2}⁡(x+z)\operatorname{cos}⁡(z-3y)\,dV={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
